To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the relationship between perceived self efficacy and entrepreneurial intention is stronger in women than in men.

the relationship between perceived behavioral control, specifically perceived self efficacy, and entrepreneurial intention is stronger in men, and that the relationship between intention and entrepreneurial behavior is stronger in women.
the dimensions of entrepreneurial intention are not the same for men and women; and that gender is a mediator in the translation of intentions into actions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of affect in entrepreneurial intention and with gender differences in the entrepreneurial intention formation.
gender differences in entrepreneurial intention and the role that attitude and perceived behavioral control play in the formation of intention.
the development and validation of a model of entrepreneurial intention that incorporates the dimensions of the attitude, perceived behavioral control and entrepreneurial intention constructs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this research provides evidence that gender differences exist in the levels of attitude toward entrepreneurship and perceived behavioral control, in the relationships between these two variables and entrepreneurial intention, and in the relationships between commitment to entrepreneurship intention and nascent entrepreneurship intention.

gender is not a moderator in the relationship between entrepreneurial intention and entrepreneurial action, but rather it is a moderator of intention action translation, thus highlighting the need for future research to focus more on the intention action translation.

this study contributes to the literature on entrepreneurship and gender in two important ways: (1) by providing evidence that attitude, perceived behavioral control and entrepreneurial intention consist of more than one dimension; and (2) by revealing gender related differences in these constructs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

this study contributes to the literature on entrepreneurship by providing empirical support to the theory of planned behaviour and by revealing gender related differences in attitude, perceived behavioral control and entrepreneurial intention.
gender related differences exist not only in the level of entrepreneurial intention but also in the interrelationships between its determinants.
gender differences in the levels and the interrelations of attitude toward entrepreneurship, self efficacy, and entrepreneurial intention are important to consider in the entrepreneurial process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the theory of planned behaviour is a powerful tool for understanding the entrepreneurial process, and that the gender related differences in this process are not as pronounced as one would expect.
the gender related differences in entrepreneurship are complex and that they cannot be fully explained by the traditional approach that focuses on the differences in the levels between the sexes.

the entrepreneurial intention is a complex multidimensional concept and the gender related differences in its components and interrelations with other variables should be taken into consideration in future entrepreneurship research and practice.
